newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine constitution amendment row hots up.
newsitem.headline: Philippine constitution amendment row hots up.

text.p: A new opposition group was launched in the Philippines on Friday in order to resist moves to amend the constitution and allow President Fidel Ramos to run for a second term.

"No to charter change! No to a new dictatorship," said a full page newspaper advertisement issued by the group, called People Resist. It claimed the membership of prominent politicians and hundreds of citizens, including churchmen.
"Eleven years ago, the Filipino people overthrew the hated Marcos dictatorship. We rose up as one people to win back our future and uphold our basic freedoms.
"Today, we are challenged anew to stand up in unity against a conspiracy to restore authoritarian rule," the advertisement in the Philippine Daily Inquirer said.
Ramos has repeatedly said he does not want to stand for elections in 1998 but his protestations have only drawn suspicion as his aides have continued to talk about constitutional amendments.

The Philippine Constitution, framed after late President Ferdinand Marcos was ousted after 20 years in office by a popular uprising, limits a president to only one term of six years. The limit is intended as a safeguard against authoritarian rule.

A group calling itself the People's Initiative for Reform, Modernization and Action (Pirma) has in the past several weeks been collecting signatures in a bid to force a plebiscite on the constitutional amendment.
"No to the Ramos-engineered charter change," said the advertisement put out by People Resist, which described itself as a group of "people against rising tyranny."
